{{Year in Israel|2000}}
Events in the year '''2000 in [[Israel]]'''.

==Incumbents==
* [[President of Israel]] – [[Ezer Weizman]] to July 13, [[Avraham Burg]] acting president July 13 to August 1, [[Moshe Katsav]] from August 1
* [[Prime Minister of Israel]] – [[Ehud Barak]]
* [[Supreme Court of Israel|President of the Supreme Court]] – [[Aharon Barak]]
* [[Chief of General Staff (Israel)|Chief of General Staff]] – [[Shaul Mofaz]]
* [[Government of Israel]] – [[Twenty-eighth government of Israel|28th Government of Israel]]

==Events==
[[File:Arrow anti-ballistic missile launch2.jpg|thumb|right|March 14: Israel formally deploys its [[Arrow (Israeli missile)|Arrow 2]] anti-ballistic missile system.]]

===January===
* January 3–10 – [[Shepherdstown Summit]]: Israel and [[Syria]] hold peace talks in [[Shepherdstown, West Virginia]]. Israeli Prime Minister [[Ehud Barak]] led the Israeli delegation and Foreign Minister [[Farouk al-Sharaa]] led the Syrian delegation. The Peace Conference finally came to a dead end and was later on followed by failed negotiation attempts to renew it.
* January 28 – [[Yes (Israel)|Yes]], the sole satellite television provider ([[Direct broadcast satellite|DBS]]) in Israel, begins its broadcasting.

===March===
* March 12–26 – [[Pope John Paul II]] visits Israel, and thus becomes the second pope to visit  Israel. During his stay, the Pope visits [[Yad Vashem]] (the Israeli national [[the Holocaust|Holocaust]] memorial) and the [[Western Wall]] placing a letter inside it in which he prayed for forgiveness for the actions against Jews in the past.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/march/26/newsid_4168000/4168803.stm|title=2000: Pope prays for Holocaust forgiveness|date=March 26, 2000|publisher=BBC News|access-date=January 10, 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081218143848/http://news.bbc.co.uk/onthisday/hi/dates/stories/march/26/newsid_4168000/4168803.stm| archive-date=December 18, 2008 <!--DASHBot-->| url-status= live}}</ref>
* March 14 – Israel formally deploys its [[Arrow (Israeli missile)|Arrow 2]] anti-ballistic missile system.<ref name=tests>{{cite web|publisher=Israel Missile Defense Organization |title=Story of the Arrow weapon system |url=http://www.mod.gov.il/pages/homa/bg.htm |access-date=August 19, 2009 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090908222327/http://www.mod.gov.il/pages/homa/bg.htm |archive-date=September 8, 2009 }}</ref>
* March 27 – An [[Israeli Air Force]] F-16D-30F of [[109 Squadron (Israel)]] based at [[Ramat David Airbase]], crashes into the [[Mediterranean Sea]] during a training flight {{convert|17|nmi|km|abbr=on}} off the coastal village of [[Atlit (modern town)|Atlit]] in northern Israel. The pilot, Major Yonatan Begin, was a son of parliamentarian [[Benny Begin]] and grandson of former Prime Minister [[Menachem Begin]]. Neither he nor his co-pilot, Lt. Lior Harari, had notified their ground controllers of any problems.<ref>[https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9E04EEDB163CF93AA15750C0A9669C8B63&sec=&spon= "Grandson of Begin Lost in Israeli F-16 Crash."] ''The New York Times'', March 29, 2000. Retrieved: June 13, 2008.</ref><ref>[http://www.f-16.net/news_article518.html "F-16 Crash."] ''f-16.net''. Retrieved: October 25, 2009.</ref>
* March 28 – A police investigation recommends that former prime minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] and his wife be indicted on criminal charges of fraud, bribery, theft of state gifts and obstruction of justice.<ref>JoPS. Page 177. source given as New York Times, Washington Post 3/29.</ref>

===May===
* 13 May – [[PingPong (band)|Ping Pong]] represents [[Israel in the Eurovision Song Contest 2000|Israel at the Eurovision Song Contest]] with the song “[[Sameach]]” ("Happy").<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diggiloo.net/?2000il|title= 2000 Israel – Sameyach|website=Diggiloo Thrush|access-date=2021-07-30}}</ref>
* May 25 – [[Israeli occupation of Southern Lebanon (1982–2000)#2000 Israeli withdrawal|Israel withdraws IDF forces from the "security zone" in southern Lebanon]], in compliance with [[U.N. Resolution 425]], to the international border after 22 years in which the area was occupied by Israeli forces. Several thousand members of the [[South Lebanon Army]] (and their families) withdraw to Israel as well with the Israeli forces. [[Syria]] and [[Lebanon]] insist that the withdrawal is incomplete, claiming the [[Shebaa Farms]] as Lebanese and still under occupation. The UN certifies full Israeli withdrawal.

===June===
* June 16 –  [[Israel]] complies with [[UN Security Council Resolution 425]] after 22 years of it issuance, which calls on Israel to completely withdraw from [[Lebanon]]. Israel withdraws from all of Lebanon, except the disputed Shebba farms.

===July===
* July 13 – [[Ezer Weizman]] resigns as president. [[List of Knesset speakers|Knesset Speaker]], [[Avraham Burg]] is appointed as acting president.
* July 31 – The Israeli [[Knesset]] elects [[Moshe Katsav]] as the [[List of Presidents of Israel|eighth president of the State of Israel]], by a majority of 63 to 57, against [[Shimon Peres]], to assume office on August 1, 2000.

===August===
* August 1 – [[Moshe Katsav]] assumes office as the [[List of Presidents of Israel|eighth president]] of the State of Israel.

===September===
* September 3 – Former leader of Israel's [[Shas|Shas Party]] [[Aryeh Deri]] starts his three-year jail sentence after his appeal is rejected.

===October===
* October 1–9, 2000: Solidarity demonstrations held by Arab citizens of Israel escalate into clashes with Israeli police and Israeli Jewish citizens. Twelve [[Arab citizens of Israel|Israeli Arabs]] and one Palestinian Arab from the [[Gaza Strip]] are shot and killed by the Israeli police.<ref>{{cite web|title=Extremism isn't Growing, but Fear is|author=Yair Ettinger|publisher=Ha'aretz|access-date=February 20, 2006|url=https://www.haaretz.com/hasen/pages/ShArt.jhtml?itemNo=431598&contrassID=2&subContrassID=20&sbSubContrassID=0&listSrc=Y|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001045335/http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/pages/ShArt.jhtml?itemNo=431598&contrassID=2&subContrassID=20&sbSubContrassID=0&listSrc=Y|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 1, 2007}}</ref> One [[Israeli Jew]]ish civilian was killed by a rock thought to have been thrown by an Arab citizen.
* October 7 – [[2000 Hezbollah cross-border raid]]: Three Israeli soldiers are abducted by Hezbollah while patrolling the Israeli administered side of the [[Blue Line (Lebanon)|Israeli-Lebanese border]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mfa.gov.il/MFA/MFAArchive/2000_2009/2001/2/Israelis%20Held%20by%20the%20Hizbullah%20-%20Oct%202000-Jan%202004 |title=Israelis Held by the Hizbullah – Oct 2000 – Jan 2004 |work=[[mfa.gov.il]] |access-date=19 July 2010 |url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070210042657/http://www.mfa.gov.il/MFA/MFAArchive/2000_2009/2001/2/Israelis%20Held%20by%20the%20Hizbullah%20-%20Oct%202000-Jan%202004 |archive-date=February 10, 2007 }}</ref> and Northern Israel is shelled in an attempt to ignite the Israeli-Lebanese border too, but Israelis decide on limited response.

===December===
* December 10 – Prime minister [[Ehud Barak]] announces his resignation as prime minister, and states that an election for the post would be held soon.

=== Israeli–Palestinian conflict ===
[[File:President Clinton walks with Prime Minister Ehud Barak of Israel and Yasser Arafat of the Palestinian Authority on the grounds of Camp David - DPLA - 0810914d4d68fc753b34c9e36003daa1.jpg|thumb|200px|right|[[Ehud Barak]], [[Bill Clinton]], and [[Yasser Arafat]] during the [[2000 Camp David Summit]]]]

====July====
* July 11–25 – The [[Camp David 2000 Summit]] is held which is aimed at reaching a "final status" agreement. The summit collapses after [[Yasser Arafat]] would not accept a proposal drafted by American and Israeli negotiators. [[Ehud Barak]] is prepared to offer the entire [[Gaza Strip]], part of East [[Jerusalem]] as capital of a Palestinian Arab state, 73% of the [[West Bank]] (excluding eastern Jerusalem) raising to 90–94% after 10–25 years, and financial reparations for Palestinian Arab refugees for peace. Arafat turns down the offer without making a counter-offer.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mideastweb.org/campdavid2.htm |title=Camp David Proposals for Final Palestine-Israel Peace Settlement |access-date=August 11, 2010 |archive-date=October 22, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022072323/http://www.mideastweb.org/campdavid2.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* September 28 – Israeli opposition leader [[Ariel Sharon]] visits the [[Temple Mount]], protected by a several-hundred-strong Israeli police force. Riots by Palestinian Arabs erupt, leading to a full-fledged armed uprising (called the [[Al-Aqsa Intifada]] by sympathizers and the [[Oslo War]] by opponents).

====October====
* October 12 – [[2000 Ramallah lynching]] – A [[Palestinian people|Palestinian Arab]] [[Crowd|mob]] lynches two [[Israel Defense Forces]] [[reservist]]s, Vadim Nurzhitz and Yossi Avrahami, who had accidentally entered the [[Palestinian National Authority|Palestinian Authority]]-controlled city of [[Ramallah]] in the [[West Bank]]. The brutality of the event, captured in a photo of one of the perpetrators proudly waving his blood-stained hands to the crowd below, sparks international outrage and further intensifies the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestinian Arabs.

'''Notable Palestinian militant operations against Israeli targets'''<br />
{{Main|Palestinian political violence#Second Intifada (2000–2005)|List of Palestinian suicide attacks#2000 (5 bombings)|Violence in the Israeli–Palestinian conflict 2000}}
The most prominent [[Palestinian political violence|Palestinian militant acts and operations]] committed against Israeli targets during 2000 include:

* November 2 – 2 Israelis are killed and 10 are wounded when a car bomb explodes near the [[Mahane Yehuda Market]] in [[Jerusalem]], one of whom is the daughter of the MK and former housing minister [[Yitzhak Levy]]. [[Islamic Jihad Movement in Palestine|Islamic Jihad]] claims responsibility for the attack.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/1004099.stm |work=BBC News | title=Bomb kills two in Jerusalem | date=November 2, 2000| access-date= 29 December 2010 <!--DASHBot-->}}</ref>
* November 20 – [[Kfar Darom]] bombing: an Israeli school bus was struck by a roadside bomb at the Jewish settlement of [[Kfar Darom]] killing 2 adults and injuring several others. Hamas claimed responsibility.<ref name="NZ_Herald_160812">{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/news/article.cfm?c_id=2&objectid=160812 |title=Children hurt in fatal bus blast |date=November 21, 2000 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=September 14, 2011}}</ref>
* November 22 – Hadera's main street bombing: Two Israeli women are killed and 60 civilians are wounded in a car bomb attack in [[Hadera]]. Hamas claimed responsibility.<ref>[http://www.rte.ie/news/2000/1122/mideast.html Palestinian Authority denies involvement in bomb attack – RTÉ News]</ref>
* December 22 – Mechola bombing: Palestinian suicide bomber injures 3 Israeli soldiers. Hamas claimed responsibility.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://select.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=F20716FE3F5C0C708EDDAB0994D8404482 | work=The New York Times | title=Mideast Deaths Mount as Negotiators Meet | date=December 23, 2000| access-date= 29 December 2010 <!--DASHBot-->}}</ref>

'''Notable Israeli military operations against Palestinian militancy targets'''<br />
The most prominent Israeli military [[counter-terrorism]] operations ([[military campaign]]s and [[military operations]]) carried out against [[Palestinian militants]] during 2000 include:

* September 30 – [[Second Intifada]]: [[Muhammad al-Durrah incident]] – Ten Palestinian Arabs are killed during crossfire between Israeli forces and Palestinian Arab militia at the Netzarim junction,<ref>{{cite news|title=12-year-old boy among dead in Israeli-Palestinian cross fire| url=http://archives.cnn.com/2000/WORLD/meast/09/30/israel.palestinian.victims.ap/index.html|publisher=CNN| date=October 1, 2000|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071006114621/http://archives.cnn.com/2000/WORLD/meast/09/30/israel.palestinian.victims.ap/index.html |archive-date = October 6, 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref> among them the twelve-year-old boy [[Muhammad al-Durrah]] who is caught in the crossfire and is allegedly killed in the arms of his father.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.btselem.org/English/Statistics/Casualties_Data.asp?Category=1 |title= B'Tselem - Statistics - Fatalities|website=www.btselem.org |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080504212243/http://www.btselem.org/english/statistics/Casualties_Data.asp?Category=1 |archive-date=May 4, 2008}}</ref> Al-Durrah's death was filmed by a Palestinian Arab freelance cameraman and made worldwide headlines and as a result Al-Durrah became a symbol of the Palestinian Arab uprising in 2000 and of Palestinian [[martyrdom]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071011000810/http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/909972.html Mohammed al-Dura lives on] by [[Gideon Levy]] on [[Haaretz]]</ref> Whether the Israeli forces or the Palestinian Arab militia shot the boy is a matter of dispute.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/middle_east/7083129.stm |work=BBC News | title=Dispute rages over al-Durrah footage | date=November 8, 2007 | first=Martin | last=Patience| access-date= 26 August 2010 <!--DASHBot-->}}</ref><ref>[https://www.jpost.com/Features/Article.aspx?id=78082 Between the Lines: Caught in the Mohammad al JPost – Features]</ref>
* December 17 – [[Tanzim]] activist Samih al-Malabi, is assassinated by a mobile phone [[bomb]] near the [[Kalandia|Qalandiyya]] refugee camp.<ref>[http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=NewsLibrary&p_multi=BBAB&d_place=BBAB&p_theme=newslibrary2&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0F97E0827A6358B0&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM NewsLibrary.com – newspaper archive, clipping service – newspapers and other news sources]</ref>

==Notable deaths==
* February 23 – [[Ofra Haza]] (born 1957), Israeli singer.
* August 12 – [[Eliahu Ben Elissar]] (born 1932), Polish-born Israeli diplomat and politician.
* September 22 – [[Yehuda Amichai]] (born 1924), German-born Israeli poet and an Israeli.
* November 12 – [[Leah Rabin]] (born 1928), German-born wife of former Prime minister of Israel [[Yitzhak Rabin]].
* December 31 – Rabbi [[Binyamin Ze'ev Kahane]] (born 1966), American-born Israeli settler leader.
